entities.title: zazzle invoker benchmarks
entities.summary: Measures how long one zazzle process takes to start and finish, against a startup floor, a libc hello, grep and cat, and how long refs takes over a large tree, cold and warm.
entities.purpose: spawnbench.c spawns a command repeatedly with its output on a pipe and prints latency percentiles in microseconds (SPAWNBENCH_WARMUP sets the unmeasured warm-up runs); exit0.c is the startup floor (zazzle's own entry, exiting at once); hello_libc.c is a minimal libc program for comparison. run.sh starts zazzled on a temporary socket, writes a small tree, and times exit0, hello_libc, `zazzle version`, `zazzle find`, `grep -rn`, `zazzle read` and `cat`; `sh bench/run.sh [N]` runs N spawns of each (default 3000). refs.sh times `refs Error` and `refs Result` over the cargo registry's crate sources: cold, with a fresh `zazzled run` per run, and warm, through `zazzle` and a running daemon; `sh bench/refs.sh [COLD WARM]` (default 20 and 100).
boundaries: The numbers they print are readings; the spawn latencies quoted in macos/rust/zazzled/README.md (Measurements) name run.sh as their source. Nothing here gates a build.
`make` builds exit0, hello_libc and spawnbench into build/ beside zazzle; ZAZZLED names a zazzled other than the release build.
